before_statement:
The following elementary valuation argument is a mathematical review candidate, not a new compiled lemma. Suppose beta is positive squarefree and coprime to6, and a nonzero rational abscissa x=beta*r^2 occurs on y^2=x(x-n)(x+3n). At a prime p|beta with p not dividing n, v_p(x)=1+2v_p(r) is odd and nonzero. If it is positive, both other factors are units, so the right side has odd valuation v_p(x). If it is negative, both other factors have the same valuation as x, so the right side has odd valuation3v_p(x). Neither can be a rational square. The zero-right-side cases x=n or x=-3n have valuation0 and cannot occur here. Thus every prime in beta must divide n.

Consequently a theorem requiring every prime divisor of n to be1 or23 modulo24 cannot supply a retained beta-abscissa point when beta is17 modulo24: such primes can only multiply to1 or23 modulo24. This is an intrinsic class/support incompatibility, not just a failure to verify a hypothesis of our particular finite construction. It does not rule out other direct-rank results, actual point existence, or a different proof of the needed global input.

If it is positive, X=a-3n and X-n=a-4n are units because p does not divide6, so the right side has odd valuation v_p(a). If it is negative, all three factors have valuation v_p(a), so the right side has odd valuation3v_p(a). Neither can be a rational square. The zero-right-side cases require a=0,3n,4n and are impossible here. Thus every prime in the actual retained beta support must divide n. Consequently a theorem requiring every prime divisor of n to be1 or23 modulo24 cannot supply a retained beta-coordinate point when beta is17 modulo24: such primes can only multiply to1 or23 modulo24. This is an intrinsic class/support incompatibility, not just a failure to verify a hypothesis of our particular finite construction.
